Bayesian panel spatial probit and ordered probit models

Source: R/psprobit.R
psprobit.Rd

Fits spatial probit (psprobit()) and spatial ordered probit (psoprobit()) models to balanced panel data by Markov chain Monte Carlo. The latent outcome of unit \(i\) in period \(t\) follows $$z_t = \rho W z_t + X_t\beta + W X_t\theta + \alpha + u_t, \quad u_t = \lambda M u_t + \varepsilon_t, \quad \varepsilon_t \sim N(0, I_N),$$ with \(y_{it} = 1\{z_{it} > 0\}\) for binary outcomes and \(y_{it} = j\) if \(\kappa_{j-1} < z_{it} \le \kappa_j\) for ordered outcomes (\(\kappa_1 = 0\)).

Usage

psprobit(
  formula,
  data,
  index,
  W,
  model = c("sar", "sdm", "slx", "sem", "sdem", "sarar", "none"),
  effects = c("random", "pooled", "spatial_random"),
  cre = NULL,
  durbin = NULL,
  time_effects = FALSE,
  M = NULL,
  dynamic = NULL,
  errors = "normal",
  priors = psp_priors(),
  control = psp_control(),
  impacts = TRUE
)

psoprobit(
  formula,
  data,
  index,
  W,
  model = c("sar", "sdm", "slx", "sem", "sdem", "sarar", "none"),
  effects = c("random", "pooled", "spatial_random"),
  cre = NULL,
  durbin = NULL,
  time_effects = FALSE,
  M = NULL,
  dynamic = NULL,
  errors = "normal",
  priors = psp_priors(),
  control = psp_control(),
  impacts = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula with an intercept. For psprobit() the response is 0/1, logical or a two-level factor; for psoprobit() an (ordered) factor or integer codes with at least three categories.

data

A data frame with one row per unit and period (balanced panel). Outcomes may be missing (NA): their latent values are imputed during sampling, which keeps the spatial structure intact. Regressors may not.

index

Character vector naming the unit and time columns of data.

W

Spatial weights for the units (see psp_weights()); its row names identify the units. It is used as given, so row-standardise it beforehand (e.g. psp_weights(W, style = "W")) if desired. For weights that change over time, pass a list with one matrix per period, named by period (or in period order); \(W_t\) then replaces \(W\) in period \(t\), including in the Durbin terms and the spatially lagged outcome of psp_dynamic().

model

Spatial specification:

  • "sar": spatial lag of the latent outcome;

  • "sdm": spatial Durbin, SAR plus \(WX\);

  • "slx": \(WX\) only;

  • "sem": spatial error, \((I - \lambda M)(z_t - X_t\beta - \alpha) = \varepsilon_t\);

  • "sdem": spatial Durbin error, SEM plus \(WX\);

  • "sarar": spatial lag and spatial error;

  • "none".

effects

Unit heterogeneity: "random" (\(\alpha_i \sim N(0, \sigma_\alpha^2)\)), "pooled" (\(\alpha = 0\)) or "spatial_random" (spatially autocorrelated effects \(\alpha = \phi W\alpha + a\), \(a_i \sim N(0, \sigma_\alpha^2)\), as in Wang and Kockelman 2009; \(W\) must then be time-invariant and \(\phi\) uses rho_range).

cre

Correlated random effects: a one-sided formula (or TRUE for all regressors) giving the regressors whose unit means are added to the model (Mundlak device, columns mean_<x>), or list(type = "chamberlain", vars = ~ x1) to add the values of the regressors in every period instead (Chamberlain device, columns cre_<x>_<period>). Chamberlain needs \(T\) extra columns per regressor.

durbin

For "sdm"/"slx": a one-sided formula selecting the regressors whose spatial lags enter the model (default: all).

time_effects

Logical; add period dummies.

M

Spatial weights for the error term of "sem", "sdem" and "sarar" (default: W). Its row names must match those of W. Like W, it may be a list with one matrix per period.

dynamic

Optional dynamic specification from psp_dynamic() (lagged outcomes and initial conditions). The first period is then used only as the initial condition, and predict() returns values for the other periods.

errors

Distribution of the latent errors: "normal" (probit) or Student-t from psp_t().

priors

Priors, see psp_priors().

control

MCMC settings, see psp_control().

impacts

Logical; compute impacts (average direct, indirect and total marginal effects on probabilities) after sampling.

Value

An object of class psprobit (and psoprobit for ordered models).

Convergence

The sampler augments the data with the latent outcomes (Albert and Chib 1993), which mixes well for balanced outcomes but slowly in some situations:

  • rare outcomes (roughly under 10% in one category);

  • near-separation (outcomes that barely vary within units or periods);

  • strong latent dynamics (psp_dynamic(latent = TRUE) with \(|\gamma|\) near or above 1);

  • "sarar" with M = W.

The intercept, \(\rho\) and \(\sigma_\alpha\) are then strongly correlated a posteriori and their chains are autocorrelated. This slowness is inherent to data augmentation with imbalanced outcomes (Johndrow et al. 2019), and reparameterisations do not remove it. Run longer chains (psp_control(iter = , warmup = ), with thin to save memory) until the warning about R-hat or bulk ESS disappears.

References

Albert, J. H. and Chib, S. (1993). Bayesian analysis of binary and polychotomous response data. JASA 88, 669-679.

Johndrow, J. E., Smith, A., Pillai, N. and Dunson, D. B. (2019). MCMC for imbalanced categorical data. JASA 114, 1394-1403.

Kakamu, K. and Wago, H. (2005). Bayesian spatial panel probit model with an application to business cycle in Japan. MODSIM 2005, 856-862.

LeSage, J. P. and Pace, R. K. (2009). Introduction to Spatial Econometrics. CRC Press.

Wang, X. and Kockelman, K. M. (2009). Bayesian inference for ordered response data with a dynamic spatial-ordered probit model. Journal of Regional Science 49, 877-913.

Examples

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(5, 5), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 4, beta = c(0, 1, -1), rho = 0.5, sigma_alpha = 0.5,
                  seed = 1)
fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, index = c("id", "time"), W = W,
                control = psp_control(iter = 300, warmup = 200, chains = 2, seed = 1))
#> Warning: Possible convergence problems (R-hat > 1.01 or bulk ESS < 200) for: (Intercept), x1, x2, rho, sigma_alpha. Consider more iterations.
summary(fit)
